items.stem: A risk falls well within the organisation's stated risk appetite. The most defensible response is often to:

options.text: Accept the risk and monitor it
options.rationale: Correct: risks within appetite are commonly accepted and monitored.

options.text: Spend heavily to eliminate it entirely
options.rationale: Eliminating a within-appetite risk wastes resources.
Transfer is not justified for a within-appetite risk at any cost.

items.explanation: Correct: risks within appetite are commonly accepted and monitored.

items.stem: Which best describes 'principled performance' in an integrated GRC capability?

options.text: Reliably achieving objectives while addressing uncertainty and acting with integrity
options.rationale: Correct: principled performance integrates objectives, risk and integrity.

options.text: Maximising short-term profit regardless of risk
options.rationale: Ignoring risk and integrity is the opposite of the concept.

options.text: Running governance, risk and compliance as separate silos

options.rationale: Documentation supports, not undermines, the capability.

items.explanation: Correct: principled performance integrates objectives, risk and integrity.

items.stem: Which TWO signals best demonstrate that a control is operating effectively over time? (Select TWO)

options.text: Monitoring evidence showing the control runs as designed
options.rationale: Correct: ongoing monitoring evidences operating effectiveness.

options.text: A single sign-off from last year
options.rationale: A one-time sign-off does not prove ongoing effectiveness.
Marketing claims are not control evidence.

items.explanation: Correct: ongoing monitoring evidences operating effectiveness. Correct: independent testing corroborates effectiveness.
